spatial_entity.notes: Hittite polity context; historical polygons resolved separately through Cliopatria.

claim.summary: Hittite evidence supports a distinct enslaved category alongside other forms of dependence: specialist synthesis describes potentially chattel slaves who were priced in law and frequently employed as herdsmen, while the legal corpus also shows status flexibility and warns against treating every non-free designation as equivalent.

territorial_practice.notes: P2 recognizes repeated legal and social attestations while avoiding a claim that all Hittite non-free persons were slaves.

source.title: Slavery in the ancient Near East
source.independence_notes: Specialist regional synthesis in The Cambridge World History of Slavery.
source.reliability_limitations: Some Hittite categories are reconstructed from legal terminology and do not map cleanly onto modern slavery categories.
